covers.quote: Number each issue of a serial and include other publication information so people can find it.
Because each issue is complete in itself, you must include the following:
name of the publisher or distributor or both

rules.quote: Include all parts of the periodical
rules.violation_condition: An issue of a periodical is missing its title, year, volume or issue number, sponsoring body, publisher or distributor, copyright details, circulation restrictions or ISSN.
when: Applies to each issue of a periodical.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading, introductory instruction and checklist; this is an independent issue-completeness check, not merely a grouping heading.

covers.quote: As well as the parts listed for periodicals, it is usual for each article in a journal to have:
references as footnotes, endnotes or a list of references
extra material useful for the content.

rules.specification: Treat the listed details as recommended, not mandatory, because the body says 'it is usual'. Assess supplementary material only where useful material is identifiable; do not infer that every article needs invented supplementary content.
rules.violation_condition: A journal article lacks the recommended article details: title and author details, an abstract, references, a DOI or useful supplementary material.
when: Applies to each article in a journal.
These details are additional to the information required for the periodical.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading and article-details checklist; the body's qualified wording makes this a recommendation.

covers.quote: the periodical’s branding and contact details
information for authors on how to submit articles

rules.violation_condition: An online periodical's home page is missing its branding and contact details, editors' names, aim, article-submission information or subscription details.
when: Applies to the home page of an online periodical.
rules.why: G-1 selects the concrete home-page checklist rather than the broad accessible-formats heading.

rules.quote: If the periodical shows page numbers, use odd numbers for the right-hand pages.
rules.violation_condition: A numbered right-hand page of a periodical bears an even page number.
when: Applies to paginated print and PDF periodicals.
Does not require page numbers where the periodical does not show them.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the conditional pagination requirement in one rule; page-number parity is distinct from numbering continuity.

covers.quote: Number the pages of the issues so they continue from one issue to the next, throughout the volume.
Start each issue of a periodical without a separate cover from page 1.
The print conventions of binding and page numbers don’t apply.

rules.quote: In print and PDF periodicals, start each new volume at page 1.
rules.violation_condition: A print or PDF periodical's pagination starts a volume at a number other than 1, breaks the continuing sequence between issues within a volume, or fails to restart an issue without a separate cover at page 1.
when: For print and PDF issues grouped into volumes, start each volume at page 1 and continue the numbering between its issues.
For periodicals without separate covers, start each issue at page 1 instead.
The print pagination conventions do not apply to digital-only articles archived without pages.
rules.why: G-2 combines the numbering scheme and its different restart conditions rather than creating competing pagination rules.

covers.quote: If the issue has a cover, it will be removed when the issues are put into volumes:

rules.quote: Include the title, date of issue, International Standard Serial Number (ISSN) and sponsoring body on the outside front cover of the volume.
rules.violation_condition: The outside front cover of a bound volume is missing the title, date of issue, ISSN or sponsoring body.
when: Applies to printed issues with covers that are removed when the issues are put into volumes.
rules.why: G-1 selects the concrete cover-content instruction; G-2 records the removable-cover condition.

rules.quote: Repeat all of this information, except for the ISSN, on the first page with the rest of the essential information, such as copyright and any restrictions on circulation.
rules.specification: Check the explicitly identified information: title, date of issue, sponsoring body, copyright and any circulation restrictions. The phrase 'such as' does not establish an exhaustive list of further essential information. The ISSN need not be repeated; its presence is not prohibited.
rules.violation_condition: The first page of a bound volume is missing the repeated title, date of issue or sponsoring body, or the specified essential copyright and circulation information.
when: Applies to printed issues whose covers are removed when the issues are put into volumes.
The information is repeated from the outside front cover onto the first page.
The ISSN is excluded from the repetition requirement.
rules.why: G-2 retains the ISSN exception; the first-page repetition requirement is distinct from information appearing on the cover.

covers.quote: the volume and part number (if any).

rules.quote: Put the publication details for each issue on the cover page.
rules.violation_condition: The cover page of an issue without a separate cover is missing the title, publishing date, sponsoring body or applicable volume and part number.
when: Applies to print periodicals without separate covers.
Volume and part numbers are required only if the publication has them.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the conditional volume and part numbers within one issue-cover checklist.

covers.quote: the name of the printer, publisher, distributor or agent

rules.quote: Put this extra information on page 2 (with the contents list) or the back page:
rules.violation_condition: A print issue without a separate cover lacks the printer, publisher, distributor or agent's name, the editorial address or subscription rates on page 2 or the back page.
when: Applies to print periodicals without separate covers.
Either page 2 with the contents list or the back page is an acceptable location.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the alternative locations within one publication-information checklist.

rules.quote: Include the title, date and page number at the top or bottom of the page.
rules.violation_condition: A page of a print periodical without a separate cover lacks the title, date or page number in its header or footer.
when: Applies to print periodicals without separate covers.
The information may appear at either the top or the bottom of the page.
rules.why: This checks running page information, not the pagination sequence; G-2 retains the alternative positions.

rules.quote: Use separate ISSNs for a digital periodical and a print periodical, even if they look the same.
rules.violation_condition: The digital and print editions of a periodical use the same ISSN.
when: Applies when a periodical has both digital and print editions.
Identical appearance does not permit the editions to share an ISSN.
rules.why: G-5 distinguishes an observable identifier conflict from the separate advice about applying for identifiers.

covers.quote: Both printed and digital periodicals must tell their users how to access extra material.
Online periodicals use a hyperlink in most cases.
Printed periodicals need to tell people how to access this material if it is not in the appendices.

rules.quote: Explain how to access datasets and extra material
rules.violation_condition: A periodical provides supplementary material but does not tell readers how to access it.
when: Applies to print and digital periodicals with supplementary material.
For printed periodicals, separate access instructions are needed if the material is not in the appendices.
A hyperlink is the usual access method online, but the page does not make that method mandatory.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate the shared access-information requirement, its print condition and its usual online implementation.
